## Type

- [ ] Failing tests
- [ ] Missing tests
- [ ] Code quality (warnings, analyzers)
- [ ] Performance optimization
- [ ] Refactoring needed
- [ ] Documentation gap
- [ ] Incorrect implementation
- [x] Other

## Description

The `Test-DuplicateEvidence` function in `tools/ai/audit/_remediation-checks.ps1` decides whether a local model's claim that "this finding duplicates open issue #m" is trustworthy. It requires BOTH a matching file anchor (a repo path the finding cites) AND a matching symbol anchor (a backticked code token of the finding) to also appear in candidate #m's real GitHub title/body before accepting the claim.

Issue #1388 fixed this function by excluding two kinds of overly generic backticked tokens from counting as symbol evidence:
1. A bare `UseXxx` messaging-pattern toggle (e.g. `UseSagas`, `UseInbox` — AGENTS.md's own generic opt-in-flag naming convention).
2. A bare file name with no path prefix (e.g. `MessagingConfiguration.cs` cited without its folder).

An adversarial review of #1388 identified a third kind of overly generic backticked token that is not yet excluded: a verbatim quote of a project house rule from AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. For example, the token `EncinaError.Message` appears backticked in many unrelated findings and issues because they all quote the same house rule verbatim ("`EncinaError.Message` NEVER reaches logs, activity tags, health-check results or plaintext storage").

**The gap.** Today, a finding about `InstrumentedSagaStore.cs` leaking `EncinaError.Message` and real issue #1328 (about different files — `TransactionPipelineBehavior.cs`, `DomainEventDispatcherInterceptor.cs`, `EventPublishingPipelineBehavior.cs`, `GraphQLMediatorBridge.cs` — leaking the same message via their `Log.cs` templates) are correctly rejected as duplicates only because their file anchors do not match. If a future finding and a future candidate issue both leak `EncinaError.Message` from a shared or overlapping file, the current AND-gate (shared file + shared house-rule quote) would wrongly accept them as the same defect. This is plausible: #1168, #1173, #1259, #1274, #1319 and #1322 are all separate instances of this exact same house-rule violation in different files, and audits repeatedly revisit hot files. A shared file citation plus a shared rule quote is not proof of the same bug in that file, yet the current logic treats the rule quote as specific symbol evidence.

## Location

- **File(s)**: `tools/ai/audit/_remediation-checks.ps1`
- **Package(s)**: N/A (tooling)

## Current Behavior

`Get-FindingAnchors` extracts every backticked token as a symbol anchor except a bare `UseXxx` toggle or a bare file name. `Test-DuplicateEvidence` accepts a duplicate claim once at least one file anchor and at least one symbol anchor both match. A verbatim quote of a house rule (e.g. `EncinaError.Message`) still counts as valid symbol-anchor evidence, which could produce a false accept for two distinct bugs that happen to violate the same rule in the same or an overlapping file.

## Expected Behavior

`Get-FindingAnchors` (or `Test-DuplicateEvidence`) excludes a verbatim quote of a known AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule sentence from counting as sufficient standalone symbol evidence — or the check requires at least two independent matching symbol anchors when the only matching symbol is a quoted rule token — so a shared file citation combined with a generic rule quote never triggers a false duplicate acceptance on its own.

## Root Cause

Symbol-anchor extraction treats every backticked token as equally specific evidence. It does not yet recognize that a verbatim quote of a project-wide house rule recurs across many unrelated findings, just like the two token classes #1388 already excludes.

## Proposed Fix

One option: extend `Get-FindingAnchors` to exclude a backticked token that is a verbatim substring of a known AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule sentence. Another option: require `Test-DuplicateEvidence` to find at least two independent matching symbol anchors, not just one, when the only match is a quoted rule token. Either way, add `Test-Hooks.ps1` cases with two synthetic findings/candidates that share only a house-rule quote and a coincidental file citation, to prove the false accept is prevented.

## Priority

- [ ] **High** - Blocks functionality or causes failures in production
- [ ] **Medium** - Should be fixed before 1.0 release
- [x] **Low** - Nice to have, can be deferred

## Effort Estimate

- [ ] Small (< 1 hour)
- [x] Medium (1-4 hours)
- [ ] Large (> 4 hours)

## Related Issues

- #1388 (the fix this issue hardens; the adversarial review that found this gap)
- #1168, #1173, #1259, #1274, #1319, #1322 (repeated instances of the same `EncinaError.Message` house rule, illustrating how often such a quote recurs verbatim)
title: [DEBT] Test-DuplicateEvidence still treats a verbatim AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule quote as specific duplicate evidence
